title: Odysseus — Ritual and worship
summary: Odysseus, hero of the Odyssey, took ten years to return home from Troy. This study follows the myth into temples and festivals.
body:
Odysseus, hero of the Odyssey, took ten years to return home from Troy. His cunning — the Trojan Horse, the blinding of Polyphemus — defines him.

Myths were not entertainment; they were scripts for ritual. Odysseus was enacted in festivals, sacrifices, and mysteries that bound communities together and aligned human time with cosmic time. Viewed through a cultural lens, Odysseus is examined as a people's self-portrait — the values and fears it encodes.

Where the myth was performed, it was believed with the body, not just the mind. A fourth sub-question examines the moral the myth was meant to teach its first hearers. Related entries in this archive: Heimdall and Coyote the trickster.
